scenario_text: Build a digital customer onboarding platform for a neo-bank that supports both video KYC and document-based KYC flows. Customers must upload PAN card and Aadhaar for identity verification — PAN details should be validated against the NSDL database in real-time. Video KYC sessions must be recorded and stored for a minimum of 8 years as per RBI's KYC master direction. The system should assign a risk score to each customer based on their profile, income declaration, and PEP (Politically Exposed Person) screening results. High-risk customers must be escalated to a compliance officer for enhanced due diligence before account activation. The entire onboarding process should take no longer than 15 minutes for low-risk customers on a stable internet connection.

requirements.statement: The system shall support two distinct customer onboarding flows: video KYC and document-based KYC.
requirements.business_justification: To provide flexibility in the onboarding process, catering to customers who prefer remote video verification or those with valid documents but no camera access.
requirements.assumptions: The system has access to necessary APIs for document validation and video conferencing services.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Users can successfully initiate and complete both 'Video KYC' and 'Document Upload' flows without error messages related to flow selection.

requirements.statement: The system shall calculate and assign a risk score to each customer based on their profile, income declaration, and PEP screening results.
requirements.business_justification: Risk scoring enables the bank to categorize customers appropriately, ensuring high-risk individuals undergo stricter scrutiny while low-risk ones get faster processing.
requirements.assumptions: The system has access to PEP databases and logic to evaluate income declarations.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Given a set of customer inputs (profile, income, PEP status), the system outputs a numeric risk score and a corresponding risk category (e.g., Low, Medium, High).

requirements.statement: The system shall escalate accounts of customers identified as 'High-risk' to a compliance officer for enhanced due diligence before account activation.
requirements.business_justification: Regulatory requirement to perform Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) on high-risk customers to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
requirements.assumptions: The system has a defined workflow for 'escalation' (e.g., creating a task, sending an alert).
requirements.acceptance_criteria: When a customer's risk score exceeds the high-risk threshold, the system prevents account activation and creates a visible task/alert assigned to a compliance officer.

requirements.statement: The system shall complete the entire onboarding process for low-risk customers within a maximum of 15 minutes.
requirements.business_justification: To ensure a seamless user experience and meet competitive expectations for digital banking speed, provided network conditions are stable.
requirements.assumptions: The 'stable internet connection' assumption holds true; the 15-minute limit includes all API calls (NSDL, PEP checks) and user interaction time.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: In a performance test with stable network conditions, the total duration from 'Start Onboarding' to 'Account Activation' for a low-risk profile does not exceed 15 minutes.

requirements.statement: The system shall display a real-time progress indicator showing the current step and estimated remaining time for the onboarding session.
requirements.business_justification: To manage customer expectations and prevent abandonment during the 15-minute window, users need visibility into process status; if the connection degrades or validation fails, they need to know where they are before retrying.

requirements.statement: The system shall notify the customer via registered email and mobile number immediately upon successful completion of onboarding and account activation.
requirements.business_justification: Users need confirmation that their action was successful; without this, they may assume failure or attempt to re-upload documents unnecessarily.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow a customer to cancel the onboarding session at any point and securely delete all uploaded documents and partial data collected during that session.
requirements.business_justification: Users must have control over their personal data; if they decide not to proceed after uploading sensitive info like Aadhaar, the system must respect privacy by removing transient data.

requirements.statement: The system shall handle NSDL database timeouts or unavailability by displaying a clear error message and offering an option to retry the validation after a configurable delay.
requirements.business_justification: External service failures are inevitable; the system must not block the user indefinitely but provide a recovery path without losing their entered data.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow a compliance officer to view the full audit trail of a high-risk customer's profile, including timestamps of all checks, PEP matches, and previous escalation attempts.
requirements.business_justification: Enhanced due diligence requires context; officers need historical data to make informed decisions on whether to approve or reject an account.

issues.description: The term 'High-risk' is used in the Statement and Acceptance Criteria without defining the specific threshold or logic that determines this status. The requirement relies on REQ-005 to define the score, but does not state what constitutes a 'High-risk' classification (e.g., score > 80) within its own scope.
issues.suggestion: Define the specific risk score threshold or category mapping that triggers the 'High-risk' status in the Statement or Assumptions.

issues.description: The stakeholder field is 'Business Analyst', but the requirement lacks a specific source identifier for the 15-minute limit (e.g., 'Per Stakeholder X, Req Y'). issues.suggestion: Ensure the 15-minute limit is traced back to a specific stakeholder request or business case document if required by governance.

issues.description: The stakeholder field is 'Not specified'. The requirement states 'To manage customer expectations' but does not identify who requested this feature or which regulation/business case mandates it.
issues.suggestion: Update the stakeholder field to a specific role (e.g., Product Owner, UX Lead) or add a source reference.

issues.description: The term 'real-time' is used again without a measurable definition. Does it mean <1 second? <500ms? The requirement must specify the latency for the progress indicator update.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'real-time' with a specific latency metric (e.g., 'updates within 2 seconds').

issues.description: The term 'immediately' is vague and unmeasurable. It does not specify a maximum latency threshold (e.g., 'within 5 seconds') which is required for testing.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'immediately' with a specific time bound such as 'within 3 seconds' or 'within 500ms'.

risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (The Aadhaar (Authentication and Offline Verification) Regulations, 2021 §26(mb) (No. 2 of 2021 (K-11020/240/2021/Auth/UIDAI)) [updated 15 Dec 2025])

risk_register.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery for the system
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §28 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall have a disaster recovery arrangement with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, tested periodically under the bank's business continuity plan.

risk_register.title: Cyber incidents reported to CERT-In within 6 hours
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support reporting cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of their being noticed, with a copy to the sector regulator.

risk_register.title: Cyber security incidents reported promptly to RBI
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Cyber Security Framework in Banks §15 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall detect and log cyber security incidents and support reporting them to RBI (and CERT-In) within the mandated timelines.

risk_register.title: ICT system logs kept for a rolling 180 days within India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(iv) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep logs of all its ICT components securely for a rolling 180 days, within India, and make them available to CERT-In on request.

risk_register.title: Identity information from Aadhaar authentication kept confidential and protected
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (The Aadhaar (Authentication and Offline Verification) Regulations, 2021 §30(e) (No. 2 of 2021 (K-11020/240/2021/Auth/UIDAI)) [updated 15 Dec 2025])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
